answer.rationale: Hard constraint is no added delivery risk with the line at 94% and no buffer and the primary contract lapsing in 14 days without auto-renew. That rules out switch and defer as first moves: even if memory_c2’s low-cost move was cheap last year, a primary cutover in two weeks would raise interruption risk, and memory_c5’s month-to-month path was for a non-critical service. Incumbent already refused to reopen price, so negotiate_terms and memory_c4/c6 volume-term savings are not available this cycle. Adding a second source (memory_c3) does not itself cover the expiring primary. memory_c1 is the only path that historically kept integration and deliveries intact; renew the incumbent for continuity and treat the 18% spend cut as unmet residual risk, not as license to break the line. Verifying c1 and c2 so a genuinely short, proven onboarding window could still flip the call.
